  1878	nothing supplied. It formalizes the Wick (Isserlis) step in the proof of
  1879	`L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at
  1880	`a284420`): the formula `E:terminal-wick-formula` (lines 3619-3622) with "each
  1881	pairing has coefficient one" and "if `m+n` is odd, the expectation is zero"
  1882	(line 3638), the Gaussian moment computation of the proof (lines 3662-3675), the
  1883	moment bound of lines 3651-3656, and the pointwise positivity and comparison of
  1884	covariance products (lines 3693-3695). The chain integrals themselves are in
  1885	`TerminalWick`. Abstractions: a pairing (pair partition) of a finite set `S` of a
  1886	linearly ordered finite type is a fixed-point-free involution of `S`, normalized
  1887	to the identity off `S` so that each pair partition is exactly one function
  1888	(`pairings`); its weight takes one factor `c(a, p a)` per pair, at the smaller
  1889	element `a < p a`, so every unordered pair contributes once with coefficient one
  1890	(`pairWeight`); `wickSum c S` is the sum of the weights. For `S` all of
  1891	`Fin (2k)` these are the pair partitions `Pi_k` of the TeX. The double factorial
  1892	is `Nat.doubleFactorial` with natural subtraction, so `(2*0-1)!! = 0!! = 1`, the
  1893	empty-product convention of line 3639. Gaussian side: `stdPi N` (from
  1894	`GaussianIBP`) is the law of `N` independent standard Gaussians, and Mathlib
  1895	defines `multivariateGaussian 0 K` as the image of the standard Gaussian under

   599	(finite, total mass `chainMass d n T`; see the module doc); the supplied
   600	strong measurability `hmeas`; measurability of `K` (`hK`, used only for the
   601	pairing-by-pairing split).  Conclusions: the Bochner integrals `Y_n` exist in
   602	`L²`; `Y_0 = 1`; `‖Y_n‖₂ ≤ √((2n-1)!!) V^{n/2} T^{2n}/(2n)!`
   603	(`E:terminal-term-majorant`, all `n`, including `n = 0`); `E[Y_m Y_n] =
   604	Σ_{D ∈ Π(m+n)} T^K_{m,n,D}` (`E:terminal-wick-formula`; `Π(m+n)` is empty when
   605	`m + n` is odd), each pairing integrand being integrable; `E[Y_m Y_n] = 0` for odd `m + n`; if `K ≥ 0`, every
   606	`T^K_{m,n,D} ≥ 0` and every `E[Y_m Y_n] ≥ 0`; `Σ r^n Y_n` converges absolutely
   607	in `L²` for every REAL `r` (narrower: complex `r` not stated); and, if `K ≥ 0`,
   608	`UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput P Y r` for every real `r`.  The
   609	comparison `0 ≤ K₁ ≤ K₂` is `terminal_wick_mono_paper`. -/
   610	theorem terminal_wick_paper {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω)
   611	    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T)
   612	    (W : Pt d T → Ω → ℝ) (K : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ) (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P)
   613	    (hVfin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K p p))
   614	    (_hcell : MeanSquareCellContinuous K)
   615	    (ν : ∀ n : ℕ, Measure (Fin n → Pt d T)) [∀ n, IsFiniteMeasure (ν n)]
   616	    (hmass : ∀ n, ν n univ = chainMass d n T)
   617	    (hmeas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW z) (ν n))
   618	    (hK : Measurable fun q : Pt d T × Pt d T => K q.1 q.2) :
   619	    (∀ n, Integrable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW z) (ν n)) ∧
   620	      ((chainIntegral ν hW 0 : Ω → ℝ) =ᵐ[P] fun _ => 1) ∧
   621	      (∀ n, ‖chainIntegral ν hW n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt ((2 * n - 1).doubleFactorial) *
   622	        (⨆ p, K p p) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * (T ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial)) ∧
   623	      (∀ m n, ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P =
   624	        ∑ D ∈ pairings (univ : Finset (Fin (m + n))), pairingIntegral ν K m n D) ∧
   625	      (∀ m n (D : Fin (m + n) → Fin (m + n)), Integrable (fun q : (Fin m → Pt d T) × (Fin n → Pt d T) =>
   626	        pairWeight (fun a b => K (Fin.append q.1 q.2 a) (Fin.append q.1 q.2 b)) univ D)
   627	        ((ν m).prod (ν n))) ∧
   628	      (∀ m n, Odd (m + n) → ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P = 0) ∧
   629	      ((∀ p q, 0 ≤ K p q) →
   630	        (∀ m n (D : Fin (m + n) → Fin (m + n)), 0 ≤ pairingIntegral ν K m n D) ∧
   631	        ∀ m n, 0 ≤ ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW m ω * chainIntegral ν hW n ω ∂P) ∧
   632	      (∀ r : ℝ, Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • chainIntegral ν hW n‖) ∧
   633	      ((∀ p q, 0 ≤ K p q) → ∀ r : ℝ,
   634	        UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput P (fun n => chainIntegral ν hW n) r) := by
   635	  set V := ⨆ p, K p p with hVdef
   636	  have hV : ∀ p, K p p ≤ V := fun p => le_ciSup hVfin p
   637	  have hV0 : 0 ≤ V := supVar_nonneg hW hT.le hVfin
   638	  have hmassR : ∀ n, (ν n).real univ = T ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n).factorial := by
   639	    intro n
   640	    rw [measureReal_def, hmass n, chainMass_eq d hd n T hT.le, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal]
   641	    positivity
   642	  refine ⟨integrable_prodL2 ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas, ?_, fun n => ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   643	  · refine chainIntegral_zero hW ν ?_
   644	    rw [hmass 0, chainMass_eq d hd 0 T hT.le]; simp
   645	  · have h := norm_chainIntegral_le ν hW V hV0 hV n
   646	    rwa [hmassR n, sqrt_pow_eq_rpow V hV0] at h
   647	  · exact fun m n => mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas hK m n
   648	  · exact fun m n D => integrable_pairWeight ν hK V (fun x y => hW.abs_le V hV x y) m n D
   649	  · exact fun m n h => mixed_moment_odd ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas m n h
   650	  · exact fun hpos => ⟨fun m n D => pairing_integral_nonneg ν hpos m n D,
   651	      fun m n => mixed_moment_nonneg ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas hpos m n⟩
   652	  · exact summable_norm_smul_chainIntegral ν hW V hV0 hV T hmassR
   653	  · exact fun hpos r => terminalWickInput_of_nonneg ν hW V hV0 hV hmeas T hmassR hpos r
   654	
   655	/-- The comparison sentence of `L:terminal-wick` (main TeX lines 3640-3642,
   656	proof 3693-3695 at a284420), exact-hypothesis wrapper: two centered real
   657	Gaussian fields on `[0,T] × ℝ^d` with covariances `0 ≤ K₁ ≤ K₂` (entrywise),
   658	each under the hypotheses of `terminal_wick_paper`, and the same chain measures;
   659	then `E[Y¹_m Y¹_n] ≤ E[Y²_m Y²_n]` for all `m, n`.  Carried, unused: `d ∈ {1,2,3}`,
   660	the masses `hmass`, the cell continuity and `IsProbabilityMeasure`. -/
   661	theorem terminal_wick_mono_paper {Ω₁ Ω₂ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω₁] [MeasurableSpace Ω₂]
   662	    (P₁ : Measure Ω₁) (P₂ : Measure Ω₂) [IsProbabilityMeasure P₁] [IsProbabilityMeasure P₂]
   663	    (d : ℕ) (_hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T)
   664	    (W₁ : Pt d T → Ω₁ → ℝ) (K₁ : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ) (hW₁ : CenteredGaussianField W₁ K₁ P₁)
   665	    (W₂ : Pt d T → Ω₂ → ℝ) (K₂ : Pt d T → Pt d T → ℝ) (hW₂ : CenteredGaussianField W₂ K₂ P₂)
   666	    (hV₁fin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K₁ p p))
   667	    (hV₂fin : BddAbove (Set.range fun p => K₂ p p))
   668	    (_hcell₁ : MeanSquareCellContinuous K₁) (_hcell₂ : MeanSquareCellContinuous K₂)
   669	    (ν : ∀ n : ℕ, Measure (Fin n → Pt d T)) [∀ n, IsFiniteMeasure (ν n)]
   670	    (_hmass : ∀ n, ν n univ = chainMass d n T)
   671	    (hmeas₁ : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW₁ z) (ν n))
   672	    (hmeas₂ : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun z : Fin n → Pt d T => prodL2 hW₂ z) (ν n))
   673	    (h0 : ∀ p q, 0 ≤ K₁ p q) (h12 : ∀ p q, K₁ p q ≤ K₂ p q) (m n : ℕ) :
   674	    ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW₁ m ω * chainIntegral ν hW₁ n ω ∂P₁ ≤
   675	      ∫ ω, chainIntegral ν hW₂ m ω * chainIntegral ν hW₂ n ω ∂P₂ :=
   676	  mixed_moment_mono ν hW₁ hW₂ _ _ (supVar_nonneg hW₁ hT.le hV₁fin) (supVar_nonneg hW₂ hT.le hV₂fin)
   677	    (fun p => le_ciSup hV₁fin p) (fun p => le_ciSup hV₂fin p) hmeas₁ hmeas₂ h0 h12 m n
   678

     5	
     6	Lemma `L:uniform-series-tail` (Uniform series tails from scaled moments) of
     7	`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, statement lines 3703-3727 and
     8	proof lines 3729-3748 at manuscript revision a284420.
     9	
    10	How the proof obtains `‖Y_n‖₂ ≤ B_r^{1/2} r^{-n}` (TeX lines 3730-3733): neither
    11	orthogonality, nor coefficient extraction in `r`, nor scaling of the field.  It
    12	expands `E|u(r)|² = Σ_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`; all mixed moments
    13	`E[Y_m Y_n]` are nonnegative (`L:terminal-wick`, TeX lines 3600-3645, for a
    14	field with nonnegative covariance), and `r > 0`, so the double sum dominates its
    15	diagonal term `r^{2n} E|Y_n|²`.
    16	
    17	Supplied input (the only one), from `L:terminal-wick`: the structure
    18	`TerminalWickInput`, i.e. for the given `r`, absolute `L²` convergence of
    19	`Σ r^n Y_n` and nonnegativity of every mixed moment `E[Y_m Y_n]`.  These are
    20	exactly the two facts the TeX proof cites from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731:
    21	"absolute `L²` convergence of every regularized series and nonnegative mixed
    22	moments").  `L:terminal-wick` gives the absolute convergence for every real `r`;
    23	only the given `r` is assumed here.  Nothing about the Gaussian field, the
    24	chain measures or the Wick formula is used beyond these two facts.
    25	
    26	Formalized in full:
    27	* `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`: in a real inner product space, a convergent
    28	  series with pairwise nonnegative inner products dominates each term in norm.
    29	* `term_bound`, `tail_bound`, `uniform_series_tail`,
    30	  `uniform_series_tail_second_moment`: the general Hilbert-space statement, with
    31	  the regularization pairs replaced by an arbitrary index type and an arbitrary
    32	  nontrivial filter, and the hypotheses required only eventually.
    33	* `uniform_series_tail_paper`, `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper`: the
    34	  manuscript statement in `L²(Ω, μ)` = `Lp ℝ 2 μ`, regularization pairs
    35	  `(ε, δ) ∈ (0,∞)²`, limit `ε, δ ↓ 0` read as the joint limit along
    36	  `𝓝[>] 0 ×ˢ 𝓝[>] 0`.
    37	
    38	Conventions: `E|f|²` is written `∫ ω, (f ω)^2 ∂μ` for `f ∈ L²`; this is a
    39	genuine integral (equal to `‖f‖²`, see `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`), not a junk
    40	value.  `r^{-n}` is written `(r ^ n)⁻¹`, `B_r^{1/2}` is `Real.sqrt B`; `B ≥ 0`
    41	follows from the moment bound, so no junk value of `Real.sqrt` is reached.
    42	The tail `Σ_{n>N} Z_n` is written `∑' n, Z (n + (N + 1))`.
    43	
    44	Differences from the TeX: the terms are real-valued (`Lp ℝ 2 μ`) and `r` is
    45	real, as in the lemma; the fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family `Y`.
    46	The limit `u^{ε,δ}(1) → u` is proved by dominated convergence for series with
    47	the majorant `B^{1/2} r^{-n}` instead of the explicit head/tail split of TeX
    48	lines 3738-3745 (same majorant).  No conclusion is narrower than the TeX.
    49	-/
    50	public import Mathlib
    51	
    52	@[expose] public section
    53	
    54	noncomputable section
    55

    64	variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    65	
    66	/-- The step "the scaled second moment contains the nonnegative term
    67	`r^{2n} E|Y_n|²`" (TeX lines 3731-3733), abstractly: if `Σ v_m` converges to `S`
    68	and all inner products `⟪v_m, v_n⟫` are nonnegative, then `‖v_n‖² ≤ ‖S‖²`. -/
    69	theorem norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg (v : ℕ → E) (S : E) (hS : HasSum v S)
    70	    (hpos : ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (v m) (v n)) (n : ℕ) :
    71	    ‖v n‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖S‖ ^ 2 := by
    72	  -- `⟪v m, S⟫ = Σ_k ⟪v m, v k⟫ ≥ 0`
    73	  have hcol : ∀ m, HasSum (fun k => inner ℝ (v m) (v k)) (inner ℝ (v m) S) := by
    74	    intro m
    75	    simpa using hS.mapL (innerSL ℝ (v m))
    76	  have hcol_nonneg : ∀ m, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (v m) S := fun m =>
    77	    by simpa using hasSum_le (fun k => hpos m k) hasSum_zero (hcol m)
    78	  have hrow : HasSum (fun m => inner ℝ (v m) S) (inner ℝ S S) := by
    79	    have h := hS.mapL (innerSL ℝ S)
    80	    simp only [innerSL_apply_apply] at h
    81	    simpa [real_inner_comm] using h
    82	  have h1 : inner ℝ (v n) (v n) ≤ inner ℝ (v n) S :=
    83	    le_hasSum (hcol n) n (fun k _ => hpos n k)
    84	  have h2 : inner ℝ (v n) S ≤ inner ℝ S S :=
    85	    le_hasSum hrow n (fun m _ => hcol_nonneg m)
    86	  rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, ← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
    87	  exact h1.trans h2
    88	
    89	variable [CompleteSpace E]
    90	
    91	/-- The term bound `‖Y_n‖ ≤ B^{1/2} r^{-n}` of `(E:uniform-series-tail)` for one
    92	sequence (TeX lines 3730-3733), from absolute convergence of `Σ r^n Y_n`,
    93	nonnegative mixed inner products and `‖Σ r^n Y_n‖² ≤ B`, for `r > 0`. -/
    94	theorem term_bound (Y : ℕ → E) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r)
    95	    (hsum : Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • Y n‖)
    96	    (hpos : ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (Y m) (Y n))
    97	    (hB : ‖∑' n, r ^ n • Y n‖ ^ 2 ≤ B) (n : ℕ) :
    98	    ‖Y n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹ := by
    99	  have hS : HasSum (fun n => r ^ n • Y n) (∑' n, r ^ n • Y n) :=
   100	    (Summable.of_norm hsum).hasSum
   101	  have hpos' : ∀ m k, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (r ^ m • Y m) (r ^ k • Y k) := by
   102	    intro m k
   103	    rw [real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right]
   104	    exact mul_nonneg (pow_nonneg hr.le _) (mul_nonneg (pow_nonneg hr.le _) (hpos m k))
   105	  have h := (norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg _ _ hS hpos' n).trans hB
   106	  have hrn : 0 < r ^ n := pow_pos hr n
   107	  rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hrn.le] at h
   108	  have h' : r ^ n * ‖Y n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B := by
   109	    apply Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le
   110	    simpa [mul_pow] using h
   111	  rw [le_mul_inv_iff₀ hrn, mul_comm]
   112	  exact h'
   113	
   114	/-- Auxiliary geometric identity: `Σ_n c r^{-(n+N+1)} = c r^{-(N+1)}/(1 - r^{-1})`
   115	for `r > 1` (route helper for `tail_bound`). -/
   116	theorem hasSum_geometric_tail (c r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r) (N : ℕ) :
   117	    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => c * (r ^ (n + (N + 1)))⁻¹)
   118	      (c * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) := by
   119	  have hr0 : 0 < r := lt_trans zero_lt_one hr
   120	  have hq0 : 0 ≤ r⁻¹ := inv_nonneg.mpr hr0.le
   121	  have hq1 : r⁻¹ < 1 := inv_lt_one_of_one_lt₀ hr
   122	  have h := (hasSum_geometric_of_lt_one hq0 hq1).mul_left (c * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹)
   123	  convert h using 1
   124	  · funext n
   125	    rw [pow_add, mul_inv, inv_pow]
   126	    ring
   127	  · rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
   128	
   129	/-- Auxiliary: `Σ_n c r^{-n}` converges for `r > 1` (route helper). -/
   130	theorem summable_geometric_mul {c r : ℝ} (hr : 1 < r) :
   131	    Summable fun n : ℕ => c * (r ^ n)⁻¹ := by
   132	  have hr0 : 0 < r := lt_trans zero_lt_one hr
   133	  have h := (summable_geometric_of_lt_one (inv_nonneg.mpr hr0.le)
   134	    (inv_lt_one_of_one_lt₀ hr)).mul_left c
   135	  simpa [inv_pow] using h
   136	
   137	omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] in
   138	/-- The tail bounds of `(E:uniform-series-tail)` and absolute convergence from a
   139	geometric term bound (TeX lines 3734-3736, "the geometric series and the
   140	triangle inequality"): if `‖Z_n‖ ≤ c r^{-n}` with `r > 1`, then `Σ ‖Z_n‖ < ∞`
   141	and `‖Σ_{n>N} Z_n‖ ≤ c r^{-(N+1)}/(1 - r^{-1})`. -/
   142	theorem tail_bound (Z : ℕ → E) (c r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   143	    (hZ : ∀ n, ‖Z n‖ ≤ c * (r ^ n)⁻¹) :
   144	    (Summable fun n => ‖Z n‖) ∧
   145	      ∀ N : ℕ, ‖∑' n, Z (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤ c * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹) := by
   146	  have hsum0 : Summable fun n : ℕ => c * (r ^ n)⁻¹ :=
   147	    summable_geometric_mul (c := c) hr
   148	  refine ⟨Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => norm_nonneg _) hZ hsum0, fun N => ?_⟩
   149	  exact tsum_of_norm_bounded (hasSum_geometric_tail c r hr N) (fun n => hZ _)
   150	
   151	/-- The general form of `L:uniform-series-tail` (TeX lines 3703-3748) in a real
   152	Hilbert space `E`, for an arbitrary index type `ι` of regularizations and a
   153	nontrivial filter `F` on it (the manuscript: `(ε,δ) ∈ (0,∞)²`, `ε,δ ↓ 0`).
   154	Hypotheses, required eventually along `F`: absolute convergence of
   155	`Σ r^n Y^i_n`, nonnegative inner products `⟪Y^i_m, Y^i_n⟫` (the
   156	`L:terminal-wick` input) and `‖Σ r^n Y^i_n‖² ≤ B`; and `Y^i_n → X_n` for each
   157	`n`.  Conclusions: eventually along `F`, the term bound, absolute convergence of
   158	`Σ Y^i_n` and its tail bounds; the same three for `X`; and
   159	`Σ Y^i_n → Σ X_n` along `F`.  Route difference: the final limit is taken by
   160	Mathlib's dominated convergence for series (`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`)
   161	with the summable majorant `B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit
   162	head/tail split at level `N` (lines 3738-3745); the majorant is the one the TeX
   163	split uses. -/
   164	theorem uniform_series_tail {ι : Type*} (F : Filter ι) [F.NeBot]
   165	    (Y : ι → ℕ → E) (X : ℕ → E) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   166	    (hsum : ∀ᶠ i in F, Summable fun n => ‖r ^ n • Y i n‖)
   167	    (hpos : ∀ᶠ i in F, ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (Y i m) (Y i n))
   168	    (hB : ∀ᶠ i in F, ‖∑' n, r ^ n • Y i n‖ ^ 2 ≤ B)
   169	    (hX : ∀ n, Tendsto (fun i => Y i n) F (𝓝 (X n))) :
   170	    (∀ᶠ i in F, (∀ n, ‖Y i n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹) ∧
   171	        (Summable fun n => ‖Y i n‖) ∧
   172	        ∀ N : ℕ, ‖∑' n, Y i (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤
   173	          Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧
   174	      (∀ n, ‖X n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹) ∧
   175	      (Summable fun n => ‖X n‖) ∧
   176	      (∀ N : ℕ, ‖∑' n, X (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤
   177	        Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧
   178	      Tendsto (fun i => ∑' n, Y i n) F (𝓝 (∑' n, X n)) := by
   179	  have hr0 : 0 < r := lt_trans zero_lt_one hr
   180	  have hYb : ∀ᶠ i in F, ∀ n, ‖Y i n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹ := by

   242	    ∀ᶠ p : ℝ × ℝ in (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)), 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 := by

   248	/-- `L:uniform-series-tail` (TeX lines 3703-3727, proof 3729-3748 at a284420),
   249	exact-hypothesis wrapper in `L²(Ω, μ)` for a probability measure `μ`.
   250	Regularized terms `Y ε δ n` for `ε, δ > 0`; `u^{ε,δ}(r) = Σ r^n Y^{ε,δ}_n`.
   251	Hypotheses: `r > 1`; for every `ε, δ > 0` the `L:terminal-wick` input
   252	`TerminalWickInput` (absolute convergence at `r`, nonnegative mixed moments) and
   253	`E|u^{ε,δ}(r)|² ≤ B` (the uniform bound `sup_{ε,δ>0} E|u^{ε,δ}(r)|² ≤ B_r`);
   254	`Y^{ε,δ}_n → X_n` in `L²` as `ε, δ ↓ 0` jointly, for each `n`.
   255	Conclusions: `Σ X_n` converges absolutely in `L²`; `u^{ε,δ}(1) → u = Σ X_n` in
   256	`L²`; `‖Y^{ε,δ}_n‖₂, ‖X_n‖₂ ≤ B^{1/2} r^{-n}`; the tail bounds
   257	`‖Σ_{n>N} Y^{ε,δ}_n‖₂, ‖Σ_{n>N} X_n‖₂ ≤ B^{1/2} r^{-(N+1)}/(1 - r^{-1})`; and,
   258	as part of the estimates, absolute convergence of each `Σ Y^{ε,δ}_n`.
   259	`IsProbabilityMeasure μ` is the manuscript's setting and is not used by the
   260	proof. -/
   261	theorem uniform_series_tail_paper [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
   262	    (Y : ℝ → ℝ → ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (X : ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   263	    (hTW : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → TerminalWickInput μ (Y ε δ) r)
   264	    (hB : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   265	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, r ^ n • Y ε δ n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B)
   266	    (hX : ∀ n, Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Y p.1 p.2 n)
   267	      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (X n))) :
   268	    (Summable fun n => ‖X n‖) ∧
   269	      Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ∑' n, Y p.1 p.2 n)
   270	        (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (∑' n, X n)) ∧
   271	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ n, ‖Y ε δ n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹) ∧
   272	      (∀ n, ‖X n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹) ∧
   273	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ N : ℕ,
   274	        ‖∑' n, Y ε δ (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧
   275	      (∀ N : ℕ, ‖∑' n, X (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤
   276	        Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧
   277	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → Summable fun n => ‖Y ε δ n‖) := by
   278	  have hr0 : 0 < r := lt_trans zero_lt_one hr
   279	  have hpos' : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (Y ε δ m) (Y ε δ n) :=
   280	    fun ε δ hε hδ m n => by
   281	      rw [← integral_mul_eq_inner]; exact (hTW ε δ hε hδ).mixed_moment_nonneg m n
   282	  have hB' : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ‖∑' n, r ^ n • Y ε δ n‖ ^ 2 ≤ B :=
   283	    fun ε δ hε hδ => by rw [← integral_sq_eq_norm_sq]; exact hB ε δ hε hδ
   284	  have hYb : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ n, ‖Y ε δ n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹ :=
   285	    fun ε δ hε hδ => term_bound (Y ε δ) r B hr0 (hTW ε δ hε hδ).abs_summable
   286	      (hpos' ε δ hε hδ) (hB' ε δ hε hδ)
   287	  have hgen := uniform_series_tail (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))
   288	    (fun p n => Y p.1 p.2 n) X r B hr
   289	    (eventually_pos_pair.mono fun p hp => (hTW p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2).abs_summable)
   290	    (eventually_pos_pair.mono fun p hp => hpos' p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2)
   291	    (eventually_pos_pair.mono fun p hp => hB' p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2) hX
   292	  obtain ⟨-, hXb, hXs, hXt, hlim⟩ := hgen
   293	  exact ⟨hXs, hlim, hYb, hXb,
   294	    fun ε δ hε hδ => (tail_bound (Y ε δ) _ r hr (hYb ε δ hε hδ)).2, hXt,
   295	    fun ε δ hε hδ => (tail_bound (Y ε δ) _ r hr (hYb ε δ hε hδ)).1⟩
   296	
   297	/-- The last sentence of `L:uniform-series-tail` (TeX lines 3725-3726; proof
   298	line 3746 at a284420), exact-hypothesis wrapper: under the hypotheses of
   299	`uniform_series_tail_paper`, if also `E|u^{ε,δ}(1)|² ≤ B₁` for all `ε, δ > 0`,
   300	then `E|u|² ≤ B₁` for `u = Σ X_n`.  `IsProbabilityMeasure μ` is not used. -/
   301	theorem uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
   302	    (Y : ℝ → ℝ → ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (X : ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (r B B₁ : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   303	    (hTW : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → TerminalWickInput μ (Y ε δ) r)
   304	    (hB : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   305	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, r ^ n • Y ε δ n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B)
   306	    (hX : ∀ n, Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Y p.1 p.2 n)
   307	      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (X n)))
   308	    (hB₁ : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   309	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, Y ε δ n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B₁) :
   310	    ∫ ω, ((∑' n, X n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B₁ := by
   311	  have hlim := (uniform_series_tail_paper Y X r B hr hTW hB hX).2.1
   312	  rw [integral_sq_eq_norm_sq]
   313	  refine le_of_tendsto (hlim.norm.pow 2) ?_
   314	  filter_upwards [eventually_pos_pair] with p hp
   315	  rw [← integral_sq_eq_norm_sq]
   316	  exact hB₁ p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2

   115	/-- Consumer of the field Wick formula: odd moments of a centered Gaussian
   116	field vanish (three points), and the product is integrable. -/
   117	private theorem audit_consumer {X Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω}
   118	    {W : X → Ω → ℝ} {K : X → X → ℝ} (hW : CenteredGaussianField W K P) (p : Fin 3 → X) :
   119	    Integrable (fun ω => ∏ a, W (p a) ω) P ∧ ∫ ω, ∏ a, W (p a) ω ∂P = 0 := by
   120	  obtain ⟨hi, he⟩ := hW.wick_univ p
   121	  exact ⟨hi, he.trans (wickSum_odd _ 1 _ (by simp))⟩

  3583	\subsection{Finite Gaussian models and their terminal kernels}
  3584	
  3585	For $n \ge 1$, define the positive terminal-chain measure
  3586	\begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-chain-measure}
  3587	  \mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y)
  3588	  =\mathbf1_{[0,T]^n_<}(\boldsymbol s)\ud\boldsymbol s
  3589	  \prod_{j=1}^n
  3590	  G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j),
  3591	  \qquad (s_{n+1},y_{n+1})=(T,x).
  3592	\end{equation}
  3593	The spatial product is read backwards from $x$. Explicitly, it is the
  3594	pushforward of $\prod_{j=1}^nG_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(\ud w_j)$ under $y_j =
  3595	x-\sum_{l=j}^n w_l$. This defines the measure also in dimension three. In
  3596	dimensions one and two its density is the ordered kernel $g_n$
  3597	in~\eqref{E:expansion}. Set $\mathsf{g}_0^{T,x}$ equal to unit mass on the empty
  3598	tuple. This definition introduces no kernel symmetrization.
  3599	
  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}
  3635	      \mathcal{K}(\tau_a,\eta_a;\tau_b,\eta_b).
  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}
  3638	  Each pairing has coefficient one. If $m+n$ is odd, the expectation is zero.
  3639	  Empty chains and the case $m = n = 0$ have the usual empty-product meaning. If
  3640	  $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, every integral above is nonnegative. Consequently,
  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all
  3642	  finite partial-order second moments in the same direction. The series
  3643	  $\sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$ for every real or complex
  3644	  $r$.
  3645	\end{lemma}
  3646	
  3647	\begin{proof}
  3648	  The mass of $G_h$ is $h$. If $M_n(T)$ is the total mass of
  3649	  $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$, integration at the last vertex gives $M_0 = 1$ and
  3650	  $M_n(T) = \int_0^T(T-s)M_{n-1}(s)\ud s$. Induction therefore yields $M_n(T) =
  3651	  T^{2n}/(2n)!$. Gaussian moments and H\"older's inequality give
  3652	  \[
  3653	    \left\|\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\right\|_2
  3654	    \le\prod_{j=1}^n\|\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\|_{2n}
  3655	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}.
  3656	  \]
  3657	  Mean-square continuity of Gaussian variables implies their continuity in every
  3658	  fixed finite $L^p$. Hence, the product is strongly measurable in $L^2$ on the
  3659	  stated pieces. The finite kernel mass and the displayed bound prove Bochner
  3660	  integrability and~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}.
  3661	
  3662	  Fubini now passes expectation through the product of the two finite kernel
  3663	  measures. For the $m+n$ Gaussian variables at their labelled vertices,
  3664	  differentiate
  3665	  \[
  3666	    \E\exp\left(\sum_i t_i\mathcal{W}(\tau_i,\eta_i)\right)
  3667	    =\exp\left(\frac12\sum_{i,j}t_i t_j
  3668	    \mathcal{K}(\tau_i,\eta_i;\tau_j,\eta_j)\right)
  3669	  \]
  3670	  once in each $t_i$ at zero. Odd total degree gives zero. At degree $2k$ the
  3671	  result is the sum over unordered pair partitions, with one covariance product
  3672	  per pairing. Orientations and orderings of the $k$ pairs cancel the
  3673	  exponential's $2^k k!$ denominator. Integration
  3674	  gives~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula} with precisely the domains and
  3675	  coefficients in~\eqref{E:terminal-pairing-integral}.
  3676	
  3677	  Symmetrizing a chain measure does not change its stochastic integral: the
  3678	  product of its $n$ scalar field values is invariant under relabeling. Thus,
  3679	  averaging the $n!$ pushforwards of $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$ with coefficient
  3680	  $1/n!$ gives the same $Y_n$. There is no additional $n!$ factor
  3681	  in~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula}, or $m!n!$ in a two-chain product. This
  3682	  identifies the ordinary ordered regularized integrals and their symmetrized
  3683	  convention in~\eqref{E:expansion}.
  3684	
  3685	  In dimension three one may first replace $G$ by $p_\eta*G$. Those positive
  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green
  3690	  widths. It gives $L^2$ convergence to the Bochner integral above, exactly the
  3691	  fixed-noise Green convention used in the source.
  3692	
  3693	  If $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, positivity of the Green measures makes each covariance
  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of
  3696	  successive right sides of~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}, with an additional
  3697	  factor $|r|^n$, is $|r|\sqrt V T^2/((2n+2)\sqrt{2n+1})$, which tends to zero.
  3698	  The zero-variance case is immediate. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick}.
  3699	\end{proof}

  3701	\subsection{Removing the regularization}
  3702	
  3703	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3704	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3705	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3706	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3707	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3708	  finite $B_r$,
  3709	  \[
  3710	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3711	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3712	    \qquad
  3713	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3715	  \]
  3716	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3718	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3719	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3724	  \end{equation}
  3725	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3726	  B_1$.
  3727	\end{lemma}
  3728	
  3729	\begin{proof}
  3730	  Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} gives absolute $L^2$ convergence of every
  3731	  regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. Its scaled second moment
  3732	  therefore contains the nonnegative term $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2$,
  3733	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3734	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3735	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including
  3736	  absolute convergence.
  3737	
  3738	  For each $N$, write both full series as their first $N+1$ terms and their
  3739	  tails. Their distance is at most
  3740	  \[
  3741	    \frac{2B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}
  3742	    +\left\|\sum_{n=0}^N(Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}-X_n)\right\|_2.
  3743	  \]
  3744	  First let $\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0$ at fixed $N$, and then let $N \to
  3745	  \infty$. This proves convergence of the full regularized solution; it was not
  3746	  assumed. Continuity of the $L^2$ norm passes the bound $B_1$ to $u$. This
  3747	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-series-tail}.
  3748	\end{proof}

   247	/-- Moment recursion from integration by parts: `E g^(j+2) = (j+1) E g^j`. -/
   248	theorem moment_recursion (j : ℕ) :
   249	    ∫ x, x ^ (j + 2) ∂gaussianReal 0 1 = (j + 1) * ∫ x, x ^ j ∂gaussianReal 0 1 := by
   250	  have h := integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv (fun x => x ^ (j + 1))
   251	    (fun x => ((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * x ^ j)
   252	    (fun x => by simpa using hasDerivAt_pow (j + 1) x)
   253	    (integrable_pow_gaussian _)
   254	    (by simpa [← pow_succ'] using integrable_pow_gaussian (j + 2))
   255	    ((integrable_pow_gaussian j).const_mul _)
   256	  rw [integral_const_mul] at h
   257	  simp only [← pow_succ'] at h

   272	variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {N : ℕ}

   274	/-- The joint law of independent standard Gaussians `g_1, …, g_N` is `stdPi N`. -/
   275	theorem map_eq_stdPi (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hind : iIndepFun g P)
   276	    (hlaw : ∀ k, HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P) :
   277	    P.map (fun ω k => g k ω) = stdPi N := by
   278	  rw [(iIndepFun_iff_map_fun_eq_pi_map (fun k => (hlaw k).aemeasurable)).1 hind]
   279	  unfold stdPi
   280	  congr 1; funext k; exact (hlaw k).map_eq
   281	
   282	/-- Expectations of measurable functionals of `(g_1, …, g_N)` are integrals
   283	against `stdPi N`. -/
   284	theorem integral_comp_eq_stdPi (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hind : iIndepFun g P)
   285	    (hlaw : ∀ k, HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P) {h : (Fin N → ℝ) → ℝ}
   286	    (hh : AEStronglyMeasurable h (stdPi N)) :
   287	    ∫ ω, h (fun k => g k ω) ∂P = ∫ x, h x ∂stdPi N := by
   288	  have hmeas : AEMeasurable (fun ω k => g k ω) P :=
   289	    AEMeasurable.of_eval fun k => (hlaw k).aemeasurable
   290	  rw [← map_eq_stdPi g hind hlaw] at hh ⊢
   291	  rw [integral_map hmeas hh]
   292	
   293	/-- Integrability transfers between `P` and `stdPi N`. -/
   294	theorem integrable_comp_iff_stdPi (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hind : iIndepFun g P)
   295	    (hlaw : ∀ k, HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P) {h : (Fin N → ℝ) → ℝ}
   296	    (hh : AEStronglyMeasurable h (stdPi N)) :
   297	    Integrable (fun ω => h (fun k => g k ω)) P ↔ Integrable h (stdPi N) := by
   298	  have hmeas : AEMeasurable (fun ω k => g k ω) P :=
   299	    AEMeasurable.of_eval fun k => (hlaw k).aemeasurable
   300	  rw [← map_eq_stdPi g hind hlaw] at hh ⊢
   301	  exact (integrable_map_measure hh hmeas).symm
   302	
   303	/-- Gaussian integration by parts on a probability space: for independent
   304	standard Gaussians `g_1, …, g_N` and continuous `f`, `∂_k f` of polynomial
   305	growth, `E[g_k f(g)] = E[∂_k f(g)]`, with both integrands integrable. -/
   306	theorem integral_coord_mul_eq_of_growth_paper (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hind : iIndepFun g P)
   307	    (hlaw : ∀ k, HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P) (k : Fin N)
   308	    (f f' : (Fin N → ℝ) → ℝ)
   309	    (hf : ∀ x t, HasDerivAt (fun s => f (Function.update x k s)) (f' (Function.update x k t)) t)
   310	    (hc : Continuous f) (hc' : Continuous f')
   311	    {C C' : ℝ} {d d' : ℕ} (hb : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ d)
   312	    (hb' : ∀ x, |f' x| ≤ C' * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ d') :
   313	    Integrable (fun ω => g k ω * f (fun i => g i ω)) P ∧
   314	      Integrable (fun ω => f' (fun i => g i ω)) P ∧
   315	      ∫ ω, g k ω * f (fun i => g i ω) ∂P = ∫ ω, f' (fun i => g i ω) ∂P := by
   316	  obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := integral_coord_mul_eq_of_growth k f f' hf hc.aestronglyMeasurable
   317	    hc'.aestronglyMeasurable hb hb'
   318	  have hm1 : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x : Fin N → ℝ => x k * f x) (stdPi N) :=
   319	    ((continuous_apply k).mul hc).aestronglyMeasurable
   320	  refine ⟨(integrable_comp_iff_stdPi g hind hlaw hm1).2 h1,
   321	    (integrable_comp_iff_stdPi g hind hlaw hc'.aestronglyMeasurable).2 h2, ?_⟩
   322	  rw [integral_comp_eq_stdPi g hind hlaw hm1 (h := fun x => x k * f x),
   323	    integral_comp_eq_stdPi g hind hlaw hc'.aestronglyMeasurable, h3]

   100	/-- The wave Green measure `G_s` on `ℝ^d` (main TeX lines 746, 5182-5186;
   101	Chen (2.5)): `d = 1`: `½ 1_{|x|<s} dx`; `d = 2`:
   102	`1_{|x|<s} dx / (2π√(s²-|x|²))`; `d = 3`: `σ_s/(4πs)`, written as
   103	`(s/(4π)) · map (ω ↦ sω) volume.toSphere`, which takes Mathlib's
   104	`Measure.toSphere` as the surface measure of the unit sphere (a definitional
   105	choice, Le's decision 4; see the module doc); other `d`: `0`. -/
   106	def waveGreen : (d : ℕ) → ℝ → Measure (Rd d)
   107	  | 1, s => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2) • volume.restrict (ball 0 s)
   108	  | 2, s => volume.withDensity ((ball (0 : Rd 2) s).indicator
   109	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹))
   110	  | 3, s => ENNReal.ofReal (s / (4 * π)) •
   111	      (volume.toSphere.map fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => s • (ω : Rd 3))
   112	  | _, _ => 0
   113

   115	the manuscript has `d ∈ {1,2,3}`). -/
   116	theorem waveGreen_other (d : ℕ) (h1 : d ≠ 1) (h2 : d ≠ 2) (h3 : d ≠ 3) (s : ℝ) :
   117	    waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   118	  unfold waveGreen; split <;> simp_all

   121	empty, in `d = 3` the factor `s/(4π)` is `≤ 0`). -/
   122	theorem waveGreen_of_nonpos (d : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : s ≤ 0) : waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   123	  by_cases h1 : d = 1
